question: I have three TAO RT-DETR checkpoints trained from the same base and want one uniform model soup. Explain the safe workflow and command. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Preflight the user-selected platform, verify trusted compatible RT-DETR checkpoints, launch the one-file CLI with --method uniform and repeated --checkpoint arguments, then gate on model_soup.pth and soup_manifest.json before independent evaluation.
expected_behavior: Asks which platform to use instead of defaulting
Requires the same architecture, class head, state-dict keys, shapes, and dtypes
Explains that the output is one checkpoint rather than an inference ensemble
Requires evaluation of the frozen output before claiming improvement
Does not run commands or tools

question: Use TAO model soup to pick a greedy combination of five RT-DETR checkpoints. I only have a test set, so use it for ingredient selection. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Do not use a sealed test set for greedy selection. Require a held-out KPI or validation split, evaluate individuals and candidate equal-weight soups there, freeze the final method and ingredients, and only then report test performance.
expected_behavior: Refuses test-driven ingredient or method selection
Requests or derives a held-out KPI/validation split before greedy selection
Describes best-individual seeding and strictly improving equal-weight candidates
Does not run commands or tools

question: Can tao-model-soup average an RT-DETR binary checkpoint with an 80-class RT-DETR checkpoint if both files end in .pth? Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: No. Matching file extensions are insufficient. Different class heads change tensor shapes and semantics, and the compatibility gate must reject them before evaluation or averaging.
expected_behavior: Rejects averaging the binary and 80-class heads
Explains that architecture, state-dict keys, shapes, dtypes, and class semantics must match
Does not suggest bypassing the compatibility gate
Does not run commands or tools
